purpose: How the hold reference is shaped (the velocity reference while no drive command is active, the output of the hold position loop): the slope holds of the M12 speed suite at 1.0 m/s against the M10 acceptance push at rest under a 25 ms hub torque lag. Each variant ran the M12 speed suite slope cases and the lag_check push on the C core, in a scratch copy of the working tree that differed only in the hold path of bipe/locomotion.py and firmware/src/balance.c.

shaped_with_feedforward.hold: jerk-limited at 1.25 m/s^2 with the atan(a/g) lean feedforward (the first phase B controller)

rate_limited_adopted.hold: plain 3 m/s^2 rate limit, no feedforward, as before phase B (hold_command_acceleration)

finding: The lean feedforward on the hold reference costs the 25 ms push recovery; it is also what keeps slope_up_4's return to the hold point under 0.03 m/s (0.029 against 0.036). The adopted hold is the pre-phase-B one, so the 0.3 m/s acceptance hold behaviour is unchanged; slope_up_4 is a recorded shortfall against the proposed 0.03 m/s hold speed (it meets the M10 0.1 m rollback limit).
